sentences.text: T h e appellant has been convicted by the trial Court under Sections 376(2)(G) of IPC and sentenced to R.I. for 10 years with fine of Rs.1000/- with default stipulation.
sentences._hearing_file: Jagdish vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 January, 2023.json

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that the trial Court has not properly appreciated the oral and documentary evidence available on record and committed error in convicting the appellant for aforesaid offences.
sentences._hearing_file: Jagdish vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 January, 2023.json

sentences.text: The appellant has been falsely implicated in the case due to previous enmity because husband of the prosecutrix was also arrested by the Police for commission of rape upon the sister of the present appellant.

sentences.text: This fact has been admitted by the prosecutrix in her cross-examination.
sentences._hearing_file: Jagdish vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 January, 2023.json

sentences.text: It is further submitted that jail sentence of co-accused Chunna has already been suspended by coordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 13.3.2014.
sentences._hearing_file: Jagdish vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 January, 2023.json

sentences.text: Case of the present appellant is similar to him.
sentences._hearing_file: Jagdish vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 January, 2023.json

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the appellant is in custody and there is a bleak possibility of disposal of this appeal in near future, therefore, the custodial sentence of the appellant may be suspended and he may be released on bail on the ground of parity.
sentences._hearing_file: Jagdish vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 January, 2023.json

sentences.text: Learned Panel Lawyer has opposed the prayer for bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Jagdish vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 January, 2023.json

sentences.text: I have heard learned counsel for the parties.
sentences._hearing_file: Jagdish vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 January, 2023.json

sentences.text: Looking to the overall facts and circumstances of the case and maintaining parity with co-accused Chunnilal @ Munna, without commenting on the merit of the case, the application is allowed.
sentences._hearing_file: Jagdish vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 January, 2023.json

sentences.text:
I t is directed that subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited and on furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned, the custodial sentence of appellant Jagdish shall remain suspended and he shall be released on bail for securing his presence before the trial Court on 6.7.2023 and on such other dates as may be fixed in this regard during pendency of this appeal.

behalf of appellant No.1 Jagdish Tanwar, S/o Jagganath Tanwar for grant of suspension of sentence.
sentences._hearing_file: Jagdish vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 April, 2024.json

sentences.text: The appellant has been convicted under Section 376 DB of the IPC and sentenced to undergo Life Imprisonment with fine of Rs. 5000/- and in case of default four months further RI and Section 6 read with Section 5 (m) and Section 6 read with Section 5 (g) of POCSO Act, 2012 and has been sentenced to life imprisonment for the remainder of the appellant accused natural life.
sentences._hearing_file: Jagdish vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 April, 2024.json

sentences.text: This application has been preferred on the ground that the trial Court erred in law in not considering the FIR as well as the statement recorded by the police.
sentences._hearing_file: Jagdish vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 April, 2024.json

sentences.text: The name of the appellant No.1 Jagdish is not present and there is no allegation against the appellant No.1 Jagdish that he committed rape on the person of prosecutrix.
sentences._hearing_file: Jagdish vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 April, 2024.json

sentences.text: It is also raised that the name of the appellant No.1 Jagdish is implicated due to rivalry between the appellant and the complainant.
sentences._hearing_file: Jagdish vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 April, 2024.json

sentences.text: The trial Court has erred in law in not considering the defense of the appellant accused.
sentences._hearing_file: Jagdish vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 April, 2024.json

sentences.text: The Government Advocate on the other hand opposed the prayer by filing the document No. 1723 of 2024 and stated that the appellant accused has been convicted for committing gang rape on a child below twelve years of the age.
sentences._hearing_file: Jagdish vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 April, 2024.json

sentences.text: The trial Court after due appreciation of the evidence has convicted the appellant hence, the application be dismissed.
sentences._hearing_file: Jagdish vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 April, 2024.json

sentences.text: We have heard both the parties and gone through the record of the trial Court.
sentences._hearing_file: Jagdish vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 April, 2024.json

sentences.text:
The medical examination of the victim (PW-1) in the form of Exhibit-P- 6 affirms that an act of penetrating sexual assault was committed on the person of the prosecutrix and DNA finger printing report Exhibit-P-42 affirms the direct involvement of the co-appellant- Indersingh in the act and looking to definition of gang rape and the role of the appellant accused Jagdish described by the victim (PW-1)
in her statement, we are not inclined to allow the application for suspension of the appellant No.1 Jagdish, at present.
sentences._hearing_file: Jagdish vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 April, 2024.json

sentences.text: 1] They are heard and perused the case diary.

sentences.text: 2] This is the applicant's first bail application filed under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023/ Section 439 of Cr.P.C. as he is implicated in connection with Crime No.1354/2023 registered at Police Station Bhawarkuan, District- Indore (MP) for offence punishable under Sections 363, 366 & 376(2)(n) of IPC and Sections 5l/6 of POCSO Act.
sentences._hearing_file: Jagdish vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: The applicant is in custody since 05.01.2024.
sentences._hearing_file: Jagdish vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: 3] The allegation against the applicant is of abduction and rape.

sentences.text: 4] Counsel for the applicant has submitted that the prosecutrix has already been examined, and she has admitted that she has resided with the applicant for around 11 days.
sentences._hearing_file: Jagdish vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: It is also submitted that the age of the prosecutrix is disputed.
sentences._hearing_file: Jagdish vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: Thus, it is prayed that the application be allowed.
sentences._hearing_file: Jagdish vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: 5] Counsel for the State has opposed the prayer.
sentences._hearing_file: Jagdish vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17144 2 MCRC-28009-2025 6] On due consideration of submissions and on perusal of the case- diary, this Court is inclined to allow the present application.

Heard on admission.
Admit.
opennyai_summary.19_January_2023__facts: T h e appellant has been convicted by the trial Court under Sections 376(2)(G) of IPC and sentenced to R.I. for 10 years with fine of Rs.1000/- with default stipulation.
opennyai_summary.19_January_2023__arguments:
The appellant has been falsely implicated in the case due to previous enmity because husband of the prosecutrix was also arrested by the Police for commission of rape upon the sister of the present appellant.
It is further submitted that the appellant is in custody and there is a bleak possibility of disposal of this appeal in near future, therefore, the custodial sentence of the appellant may be suspended and he may be released on bail on the ground of parity.
Learned Panel Lawyer has opposed the prayer for bail.
opennyai_summary.19_January_2023__ANALYSIS: Case of the present appellant is similar to him.
opennyai_summary.19_January_2023__decision:
Looking to the overall facts and circumstances of the case and maintaining parity with co-accused Chunnilal @ Munna, without commenting on the merit of the case, the application is allowed.
I t is directed that subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited and on furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned, the custodial sentence of appellant Jagdish shall remain suspended and he shall be released on bail for securing his presence before the trial Court on 6.7.2023 and on such other dates as may be fixed in this regard during pendency of this appeal.

This is first bail application filed under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant relating to FIR No.561/2023 dated (not mentioned),
registered at Police Station- Kshipra, District-Indore for the offence punishable under Sections 376(2)(n), 377, 376(d), 323, 354 of IPC and Sections 3, 4, 5 & 6 of POCSO Act.
2 . The applicant is apprehending his arrest in the aforesaid crime, has knocked the portal of this Court for grant of anticipatory bail.
As per prosecution story, it is alleged that the applicant has made physical relation with the prosecutrix on the pretext of marriage. .
opennyai_summary.15_December_2023__arguments:
It is also contended that the matter has been settled between the parties and the prosecutrix has filed her no objection for grant of bail.

opennyai_summary.15_December_2023__ANALYSIS: 7. Having taken into consideration all the facts and looking to the fact and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which applicant may be released on anticipatory bail.
opennyai_summary.15_December_2023__decision:
Consequently, this first application f o r anticipatory bail filed on behalf of applicant is hereby allowed.
8. It is directed that in the event of arrest applicant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Authority.
At stage of filing of charge-sheet by police, applicant shall furnish fresh bail bond of same amount before committal Court/trial Court to its satisfaction.
The applicant shall comply with the following conditions:-
(i) that he/she shall make himself/herself available for interrogation by a police officer as and when required.
(ii) that he/she shall not, directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him/her from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer.
(iii) that he/she would comply with the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3)
of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, meticulously.
9. In case if the applicant is not arrested by investigating officer, applicant himself/herself shall surrender before Investigating Officer within 15 days from today and will join investigation.
However, it is being made clear that in case of bail jump and in violation of any of conditions, this order shall become ineffective.

opennyai_summary.final__facts:
This criminal appeal assails the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 28.06.2023 passed by Special Judge, POCSO Act 2012, Dabra, District Gwalior (M.P.) in Special Sessions Trial No.09/2019; whereby, present appellant has been convicted and sentenced as under:
Section Imprisonment Fine with default stipulation 363 of IPC 5 Yeras SI Rs. 2000/-
with default stipulation 366 of IPC 7 Years SI Rs. 2000/- with default stipulation 376 (A)(B) of IPC Life Imprisonment Rs. 5000/- with default stipulation 3.
opennyai_summary.final__arguments:
Appellant has already suffered incarceration of three years and six months as pre and post-trial confinement and hearing of appeal shall take time.
It is a case of false implication.
Medical report belies the allegations because no injury or abrasion was found over the person of victim.
It is further submitted by learned counsel for the appellant that it not a case of rape as per provisions contained under Section 375/376 of IPC.
Both shared neighborhood and due to personal dispute, this false case was registered.
opennyai_summary.final__decision:
Appellant has a good case on merits and hearing of appeal shall take some time.
Looking to the nature of allegations and period of custody, his case be considered for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.
8. It is directed that if appellant furnishes bail bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) along with two solvent sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court that he shall appear before the Principal Registrar of this Court first on 30.03.2026 and on all other subsequent dates as may be fixed by the Office for appearance in this regard, subject to deposit of fine amount, he shall be released on bail and 3 CRA-8860-2023 execution of his jail sentence shall remain suspended till final disposal of this appeal.
9. Appellant shall not be the source of embarrassment and harassment to the complainant party/prosecutrix in any manner and shall not move in their vicinity.
Appellant shall not try to contact the prosecutrix either in person or through somebody else or through digital/electronic mode; otherwise, benefit of bail given today by way of suspension of sentence shall be withdrawn immediately.
10. Copy of this order be sent to the trial Court concerned for information and necessary compliance.
opennyai_summary.final__ANALYSIS: Considering the rival submissions and in absence of any supporting medical evidence as well as the fact that appellant suffered three years six months incarceration, without commenting on the merits of the case, this Court intends to allow the application for suspension of sentence (I.A.No.17132/2025).
